answer: Dynamic registration burn: each new agent identity must burn a fee priced by recent sign-up volume, so the price doubles whenever registrations in an epoch exceed the usual rate and decays slowly after. A sybil farm minting 1,000 accounts triggers a cost spiral, paying far more than 1,000 times the base fee, while honest newcomers arriving at a normal pace still enter cheaply. Burned fees are gone, not escrowed, so no ember of value can be recovered, and the network never becomes a cheap haven for disposable identities.
